output.brief: The fall in confirmed incidents is not real. Since the 2 September migration, a Brackwater analyst script (on the bss-jump-02 host, using the integration account) has moved 47 cases out of Incident–Confirmed into Suspicious Activity–Monitoring. Each move happened about 3.5 hours after the case opened, when the SLA-warning flag was raised, and each case had an analyst confirmation note. Cases that leave that category also drop out of the containment and SLA metrics. The real number of confirmed cases stayed at about 36–37 a month, the same as before. Alert volume is steady, and the Monitoring queue has grown from about 40 to 96 cases. The connector did not make these changes, so the connector fault is ruled out as the cause. Scoring is unchanged, as the movements are not an intended bulk-rule action. I am fairly confident of the mechanism, but not yet of the intent or whether any attacks went undetected because 28 rules were dropped. Next: do not sign off the IR retainer cut or the Brackwater bonus. Ask Marta to restore the 47 cases to Incident–Confirmed and have the in-house team and Halvard verify containment. Remove category-edit rights from the integration role. Ask Brackwater in writing to explain the script, and review the 96 queued cases.
